doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Recording with Ray Brown and Milt Hinton; writing at the piano
summary: Ray Brown and Milt Hinton made him comfortable at his session; he writes most tunes at the piano.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This album has some great things on it. It was wonderful to see Milt Hinton and Ray Brown. That must have been quite a thrill to do.

Well fortunately it wasn’t a complete surprise because we actually played together before, before we did the album. So I kind of knew what to expect. I mean Ray is more or less my Godfather so Ray and I have been close for so long. And Milt Hinton is such a wonderful man. They made me feel completely comfortable at my session.
Do you write your tunes from the piano? Because as I was walking down the hall to find you I heard this pretty mean piano and there you were behind it.

Well more than half of the tunes that I’ve written tend to start on the piano, just because I’ve always been influenced by piano players and saxophone players. So on the piano I get to see and just hear the whole orchestra, where the harmonies and the chords are going. So most of the time they tend to start on the piano. But there’ve been a couple of songs that I’ve written that started on the bass.
